speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, please describe exactly how these symptoms started and how they have progressed over time. Additionally, could you detail your significant medical history, including any previous diagnoses or surgeries?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of feeling "drunk" and clumsiness on the right side suggest a cerebellar issue. Have you noticed any other neurological changes, such as slurred speech, double vision, or weakness on one side of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.
REQUEST TEST: CSF PCR for JC virus.

Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab for a year, and the new onset of cerebellar ataxia (unsteadiness and clumsiness), we must urgently rule out PML, a serious opportunistic infection that can occur on this medication. The MRI of your brain is critical to confirm this diagnosis immediately.
